items.key: being you: a new science of consciousness
items.text: Seth's own book laying out his biological naturalist account of consciousness, referenced for more detail on why life might matter
items.context: Being You: A New Science of Consciousness

items.key: ex machina
items.text: Film used repeatedly as illustration of the techno-rapture temptation and the 'Garland test' for perceived machine consciousness
items.context: Ex Machina

items.key: klara and the sun
items.text: Listed among cultural depictions of synthetic minds that inform the mythology of conscious AI
items.context: Klara and the Sun

items.key: 2001: a space odyssey
items.text: Cited as one of the cultural touchstones for synthetic consciousness stories that rarely end well
items.context: 2001: A Space Odyssey

items.key: frankenstein
items.text: Cited as a foundational cultural narrative about creating synthetic minds that end badly
items.context: Frankenstein

items.key: interview claiming lamda is conscious
items.text: Google engineer's claim that the LaMDA chatbot was conscious, cited as the opening example of overattributing consciousness to AI
items.context: Interview claiming LaMDA is conscious

items.key: the neural replacement thought experiment
items.text: Thought experiment used to argue consciousness is substrate independent, which Seth argues fails at its first hurdle
items.context: The neural replacement thought experiment

items.key: article on the need to take ai welfare seriously
items.text: Cited as evidence machine consciousness questions are gaining serious institutional attention
items.context: Article on the need to take AI welfare seriously

items.key: interview claiming conscious ai already exists
items.text: Nobel laureate's claim that conscious machines already exist, used as an example of the view Seth argues against
items.context: Interview claiming conscious AI already exists

items.key: what is it like to be a bat?
items.text: Provides the canonical definition of consciousness as there being something it is like to be an organism
items.context: What Is It Like to Be a Bat?

items.key: more everything forever
items.text: Describes the tendency to project consciousness into AI as a form of pareidolia, a framing Seth adopts
items.context: More Everything Forever

items.key: computing machinery and intelligence
items.text: Seeded the idea that machines might be intelligent and introduced the Turing test, contrasted with tests for consciousness
items.context: Computing Machinery and Intelligence

items.key: a logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity
items.text: Landmark paper showing networks of simplified abstract neurons can perform logical operations, foundation of neural network computation
items.context: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity

items.key: work on turing completeness of neural networks
items.text: Demonstrated that McCulloch-Pitts neural networks with tape-like memory are Turing complete
items.context: Work on Turing completeness of neural networks

items.key: neural firing associated with waste clearance research
items.text: Found some neurons fire spikes apparently to clear metabolic waste, showing neurons can't be swapped for silicon equivalents
items.context: Neural firing associated with waste clearance research

items.key: mortal computation concept
items.text: Introduced the concept of mortal computation tying algorithms inseparably to their material substrate
items.context: Mortal computation concept

items.key: what might cognition be, if not computation?
items.text: Gave the Watt governor example showing some systems act without being usefully described as computational
items.context: What Might Cognition Be, If Not Computation?

items.key: biological naturalism (theory of consciousness)
items.text: The philosophical position that properties of life are necessary for consciousness, which Seth builds on
items.context: Biological naturalism (theory of consciousness)

items.key: recent research paper on life and consciousness
items.text: Cited as further, more technical support for the idea that life matters for consciousness
items.context: Recent research paper on life and consciousness

items.key: are we living in a computer simulation?
items.text: Source of the simulation hypothesis, critiqued for assuming without argument that a running program would be conscious
items.context: Are We Living in a Computer Simulation?

items.key: lectures on ethics
items.text: Argued that treating conscious-seeming things as lacking consciousness is psychologically unhealthy
items.context: Lectures on Ethics

items.key: comments on the dangers of conscious-seeming ai
items.text: Microsoft AI CEO cited as noticing dangers of conscious-seeming AI
items.context: Comments on the dangers of conscious-seeming AI

items.key: comments on the dangers of conscious-seeming ai
items.text: AI researcher cited as noticing dangers of conscious-seeming AI
items.context: Comments on the dangers of conscious-seeming AI

items.key: ai as a mirror metaphor
items.text: Philosopher's description of AI as a mirror reflecting our digitized past, used to frame the essay's closing argument
items.context: AI as a mirror metaphor

items.key: quote on technology making us forget what we know about life
items.text: Sociologist's remark used to close the essay's argument about remembering what life is
items.context: Quote on technology making us forget what we know about life
